forecaster_note: Surfline Sydney forecaster: "Solid surf at exposures in the OH range, but onshore and lumpy. Look to sheltered corners." Another pulse of long-period S swell fills in and it will be way bigger than the spot forecasts suggest — exposures overhead or more with plenty of power, sheltered corners likely chest high and fun. Moderate onshore SE winds make it lumpy for most: doable but unappealing. The numbers back it — 177 kJ at 6am peaking at 229 kJ by 8–9am, then halving to 118 kJ by midday. The wind is the whole story: it was W offshore until 3am, swung SE by 6am at 9kph, and nearly doubles to 16kph gusting 26 from 9am on. Water temp is a NSW-wide station estimate, not a Dee Why reading.

wind.summary: Dawn is the only soft window — 9kph gusting 20 from 119° at 6am. By 9am it is 16kph gusting 26 from 136° SE and it stays onshore 15–16kph all the way to 6pm. No cleanup coming today: the offshore W that blew until 3am is long gone. Every hour you wait past 8am costs you face quality.

shark.summary: SharkSmart NSW layers (DPI Fisheries + SLSNSW drone) read cleanly this refresh — 660 notification records parsed — but the most recent detection anywhere in NSW is still dated 25 July, now 22 days with nothing published. That is a feed that has stopped updating, not an all-clear, so none is given. The last Northern Beaches entries were Long Reef and Dee Why on 25 July (water evacuated both times). Tap through and check the live map before you paddle out.

days.label: Today
days.note: Go early or don't bother. This is the most energy you have seen in a fortnight — 177 kJ at 6am, 229 kJ at 9am — but it arrives with a SE onshore that goes from 9kph at dawn to 16kph gusting 26 by 9am and never lets up. Surfline has every spot at poor–fair from 6am purely on wind; the water itself is not the problem. Two swells in play: 5.4ft @ 6s from 147° doing the lumping, and a 2.4ft @ 17s from 184° underneath doing the real work — that long-period south is what the forecaster means by "way bigger than spot forecasts suggest". Your play is the sheltered corner, not the open beach: Dee Why Point, in the water by 7am, out by 9:30. The 4:27am low filling to a 10:37am high is exactly the tide that bank wants. Skip the mid-morning slot you normally like — by 10am the wind has won.

dee-why.window: 7am–9:30am. Wind is 9kph at 6am and 16kph gusting 26 by 9am — that gap is the whole session. Tide filling off the 4:27am low toward the 10:37am high, which is the Point's tide.

tip.label: The Point is the answer — and 17s changes the 184° rule
tip.text: Normally 184° is the door you don't want at Dee Why: dead south goes fat and gutless. But this one is 17 seconds, and long-period south is the one south that actually bends around the headland with its energy intact instead of dumping it on the way. That is why the forecaster is calling exposures overhead. Tuck into the Point corner — it is the only place on this stretch genuinely sheltered from a 136° SE onshore, and it is your frontside. The 5.4ft @ 6s is noise: it will stack junk on the sets and make the paddle out messy, so time it between pulses. 229 kJ under your feet is real power for chest-to-head faces — expect them to hit harder than the size suggests.

long-reef.window: 6:30am–8:30am only. Biggest of the four, and the most exposed — the 136° SE is dead onshore here with no corner to hide in once it hits 16kph.

tip.label: Size without shelter
tip.text: This is where the overhead sets the forecaster mentions will actually show up — Long Reef takes the 17s south full in the chest with nothing filtering it. The catch is it also takes the SE onshore full in the chest. Before 8am, with the wind still at 9–12kph, this is arguably the best wave of the day. After 9am it is a washing machine at 229 kJ, which is not fun, it is just work. If you are not out of bed by 6:15, go to the Point instead.

curl-curl.window: 6:30am–8:30am. Same size as Long Reef, same exposure problem. North end will hold shape longest.

tip.label: Third choice today
tip.text: Curl Curl converts a 147°/184° combination into size as well as anywhere, but it has no shelter from 136° and the 6s windswell will close out the south corner from the first gust. If you drive past and the north end is organised, it is worth it before 8am. Otherwise you have burned the only clean half-hour of the day in the car.

manly.window: Skip it. Thigh to stomach while three other spots are chest to overhead on identical energy.

tip.label: Wrong day for North Steyne
tip.text: Manly is shadowed from the south by the headland and this swell is 147–184° — every degree of it comes from the direction Manly can't see. Same 229 kJ in the water, a third of the wave on the beach. The only argument for it is the SE onshore matters less when there is nothing to blow out.

days.label: Tomorrow
days.note: The energy falls off a cliff — 74 kJ at 6am against today's 177 — but the wind finally behaves at dawn. Surfline lifts everything to fair. Forecaster calls it "fun sized peaky surf, mostly onshore and lumpy, maybe a brief AM window". Direction shifts to a 3.1ft @ 7s from 102° E with the 16s south fading underneath, which is a friendlier angle than today for everywhere except Dee Why Point. Wind is 1kph at 6am, 8kph SSE cross by 9am, onshore 11kph by noon — so the window is real but narrow. Chest-to-head at Long Reef is the pick.

dee-why.window: 6:30am–9am. Near-glass at dawn (1kph) before the SSE cross fills in at 9am. Half today's energy, so pick your sets.

days.label: Weekend
days.note: Two very different days, and only one of them counts. Saturday is a write-off on size — 40–64 kJ through the morning, knee to thigh, nothing but a 2.9ft @ 4s slop swell — though the wind is a proper W offshore 8–17kph, so it will look pretty and be useless. Sunday 23 is the one to book: 314 kJ at 6am and 251 kJ at 9am off a 5.1ft @ 9s from 182°, under a W–NW offshore of 9–10kph all morning. Long Reef gets a fair-to-good rating, the only one in the eight-day run. Confidence is low this far out (33% model agreement on Sunday), so treat it as a flag to watch rather than a promise — but keep the morning free.

dee-why.window: Sun 23, 6am–10am. 314 kJ at dawn easing to 251 by 9am under a W offshore. Saturday is knee-to-thigh — don't waste the drive.
